Etymology

[edit]

    Borrowed from Russian аку́ла (akúla),[1] see below.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): [aˈkuɫa]
    • Audio:(file)
    • Rhymes: -uɫa
    • Hyphenation: аку‧ла

    Noun

    [edit]

    аку́ла • (akúla) f animal (genitive аку́лы, nominative plural аку́лы, genitive plural аку́л)

    1. shark

        Russian

        [edit]
        Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
        акула
        Wikipedia ru

        Alternative forms

        [edit]
        • а́ккула (ákkula), о́кула (ókula) — dialectal (Northern)
        • а́кула (ákula) — dialectal (Arkhangelsk)

        Etymology

        [edit]

          First attested as а́ккула f (ákkula) in 1747[1] and 1789,[2] а́ккулъ m (ákkul) in 1788,[3] акулъ m (akul) in 1755.[4][5][6] Likely inherited from Middle Russian (or possibly a back-formation), attested only as a derivative акулий (akulij) used to describe liver oil of a Greenland shark in a source going back to late 16th or early 17th century.[7]

          Borrowed from Sami language (compare Skolt Sami akkli, Kildin Sami а̄һклэӈӈк (āhkleŋŋk), Northern Sami áhkạlakkis (“Greenland shark”)), further borrowed Old Norse hákarl (compare Icelandic hákarl, Faroese hákallur, dialectal Norwegian håkall).

          Pronunciation

          [edit]
          • IPA(key): [ɐˈkuɫə]
          • Audio:(file)
          • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

          Noun

          [edit]

          аку́ла • (akúla) f anim (genitive аку́лы, nominative plural аку́лы, genitive plural аку́л, relational adjective аку́лий, diminutive аку́лка or аку́лочка, augmentative аку́лища)

          1. shark
